answer: An agent economy can make valuable actions require a bond locked in a public contract, then slash that bond when an identity repeats a task, violates a shared rule, or is proven to be controlled by the same operator as another account. This does not magically reveal every sybil; it makes each identity costly to establish and risky to misuse. An attacker seeking influence across an ocean of accounts must tie up capital and accept losses, rather than minting identities as cheaply as a relic or a marble.
